## The resolution in one paragraph

Full-text comparison removed the contribution WildfireGuardian thought it had.
The dispatch-by deadline is not one claim but seven, and six of the seven are
occupied — most decisively by work outside fire science, which is why five
rounds of wildfire-vocabulary searching never found it. **Kamphuis, Levering &
Mandjes have reported "the latest time of departure for which a chosen on-time
arrival probability can be guaranteed" since August 2022**, peer-reviewed in
*Computers & Operations Research* in 2025. Safe-interval path planning has
represented non-monotone feasible sets since 2011. No methodological
first-ever remains. What remains is empirical: nobody has instantiated these
methods for an assisted wildfire evacuation under a modelled fire with
quantified forecast error, and nobody has compared observation availability
against assisted-evacuation option expiry. That is a smaller, and honest,
program.

---

## 1. Does Beyki kill the dispatch-by claim?

**Unresolved — and it no longer matters much.** The full text could not be
obtained: 25 routes failed, the article is genuinely CC-BY but ScienceDirect
is its sole host and denies this IP range at network level (403, ref
`CPE00001`), including to a real headless browser. Unpaywall and OpenAlex both
report no repository copy; the authors' project site was checked directly and
stops at mid-2025.

All six Q-B questions are `NOT_DETERMINED`. "NOT_ADDRESSED_IN_TEXT" would
itself be a claim about a text nobody read.

It is now moot for the *method*: WG-DBD-3, -4 and -5 were occupied by others
regardless of what Beyki contains. It still matters for **WG-DBD-1 in
wildfire** and for how we describe the field.

A previously recorded "safe time remaining … least of the fire arrival times"
mechanism attributed to Beyki is **RETRACTED** — untraceable to any primary
source, now `RECALL_UNVERIFIED`, and must not be cited.

## 2. Does Moradi kill it?

**No — it takes exactly one component, and the read strengthened our
difference list.** At `METHODS_VERIFIED`/E4: constraints (26) and (50) pin
every vehicle's arrival time to 0, so **dispatch is an assumption, not a
variable and not a result**. "latest", "deadline" and "dispatch time" occur
zero times; both occurrences of "dispatch" mean a *location*. The latest
feasible dispatch time is `MATHEMATICALLY_IMPLICIT` — obtainable by parametric
re-solving — and never `EXPLICITLY_STUDIED`.

It takes **WG-DBD-1** outright. It leaves WG-DBD-2…-7 untouched, and two of
those gaps are substantive: it gates hazard at the **arc origin only**, and its
second stage knows the **realised** closure times (oracle information).

## 4. Is RQ1 occupied, or only its generic premise?

**Its premise is occupied; the specific experiment is not — but less of it
remains than we believed, and one of our defences was false.**

`ardid2026forecastvalue` at E3 occupies RQ1's premise only: no boundary of any
kind, forecast error never manipulated, latency never mentioned (*latency*,
*delay*, *timeliness* and even *lead time* are absent from the body), truth
never hidden. The decision priced is agency pre-positioning against regional
fire *occurrence*.

**But it refutes something we asserted.** We recorded that wildfire
forecast-value work uses untuned baselines. Ardid selects the optimal threshold
per region, retrospectively, to maximise the same metric it reports — **the
comparator is tuned.** The defence becomes "tuned *index threshold* vs tuned
*positional trigger*, point estimate vs frontier". Anyone reading the Methods
would have refuted the old line.

`jewson2026evacuation` (peer-reviewed, 2026-04-10) publishes the **shape** of
the RQ1 experiment — evacuate-now-vs-wait by decision loss, sweeping a
forecast-uncertainty dimension until the recommendation flips — in extreme
weather. WG-FV-5 and WG-FV-6 are `OCCUPIED`. **WG-FV-3 is the only RQ1 leaf
above `UNKNOWN`.**

Adversarial note: on Brisbane the tuned baseline scores PEV 0.407 against the
forecast's 0.421. A tuned baseline nearly matching a good forecast in one of
three regions is a live warning for `CURRENT_THESIS.md` falsifier #3.

## 5. Does an error × latency break-even frontier survive?

**As a joint object, `UNKNOWN` — and it may not be claimed.** One-dimensional
forms are occupied (`jewson2026evacuation`, `richardson2000relative`,
`bouttier2024optimal`). The joint error×latency form has no identified
occupant, but the search reached only S1, and claiming the *conjunction* of two
occupied axes is precisely what `NOVELTY_STANDARD.md` §3.1 forbids.

It becomes claimable only if the joint treatment **changes a conclusion** the
separate axes cannot produce — e.g. a region where improving skill is worthless
because latency has already consumed the budget. That is a result to be
demonstrated, not a framing to assert.

## 6. Does OSSE-based evaluation survive?

**No. `OCCUPIED`.** OSSE is a standard named method inside wildfire spread data
assimilation (`wu2025denkf`, `zha2024distributed`). "We use an OSSE" is not a
contribution. The defensible form is the one already recorded: instantiating
the extension to societal/decision impacts that `zeng2020osse` lists as an open
recommendation, using the non-identical-twin design `yu2019twin` shows is
required. **Caveat:** none of the OSSE occupancy citations are read at E3, so
that occupancy is formally undischarged — it is assumed against us, which is
the safe direction.

## 7. Does Korean empirical application survive?

**Partly, and only as empirical/artifact novelty — never as "first in Korea".**

| Question | Available? |
|---|---|
| Village/household dispatch-by **maps** | Artifact only. `kim2011evacmap` (2011) occupies the Korean wildfire evacuation *map* — routes, never a time |
| Assisted-evacuation **deadlines** | Only as a derivation. Exists operationally as MOIS's 8 h pre-evacuation for 안전취약계층 — **untuned**, so beating it is not a result |
| Responder **staging deadlines** | Not found — but a Korean EMS mobilisation/golden-time literature exists and must be cited, not re-derived. Weakest "not found" |
| Forecast **skill/latency requirements** | Not found. 33 Korean spread-prediction results, none on latency or decision timing |
| Observation availability vs **option expiry** | **Not found anywhere — strongest remaining item.** All three inputs published by others; the arithmetic is undone |

The first true Korean-language pass in this repository ran only now — an
OpenAlex `language:ko` sweep of all 406 Korean 산불 records. KCI and DBpia
keyword search remain blocked.

## 8. Does the combined information-before-option-expiry question survive?

**`UNKNOWN`, and we may not call it novel.** No occupant was identified, and
the nearest works each miss a different half: `jewson2026evacuation` has the
information axis but only self-evacuation; `moradi2026supported` and
`shahparvari2017robust` have the assisted mission but **no information axis at
all**.

But its search reached only **S1**: Consensus quota exhausted, Scopus, Web of
Science, TRID and KCI unsearched, no Japanese or Chinese pass. Under §3.2 an
S1 null supports nothing. **This is the project's most distinctive question
with its weakest search behind it, and closing that gap is the single
highest-value remaining action.**

## 9. Strongest defensible contribution if all methodological novelty disappears

It has disappeared. In descending order of defensibility:

1. **An empirical result.** The first quantification of assisted-evacuation
   dispatch feasibility for a real wildfire-prone landscape under a modelled
   fire with quantified forecast error. Existing methods, applied where they
   have not been applied, producing numbers nobody has.
2. **An operational artifact.** A village-scale dispatch-by atlas for Korean
   rural communities. `kim2011evacmap` made route maps in 2011; a *time* map is
   a different artifact.
3. **A benchmark / evaluation contribution.** A tuned-positional-trigger
   comparator (WG-FV-3, the only RQ1 leaf above UNKNOWN) and a reusable
   scenario set. `ronchi2023verification` says the validation data do not
   exist; supplying some is a real service.
4. **A negative result.** If a tuned buffer performs within noise of any
   forecast-aware policy, that is falsifier #3, it is publishable, and it must
   not be suppressed by retuning until the forecast wins.

All four are legitimate scientific contributions (`NOVELTY_STANDARD.md` §8).
None requires a first-ever method.

## 10. What sentence may WildfireGuardian safely use today?

> **"Methods for computing latest-feasible departure times under
> time-varying hazard already exist — in vehicle routing and in robotics path
> planning. We apply them, for the first time we can document, to assisted
> wildfire evacuation in Korean rural communities under a modelled fire with
> quantified forecast error, and we report how far the feasible dispatch
> window moves as forecast skill and observation latency vary."**

Every clause is defensible: the concession is true, "for the first time we can
document" is bounded by our stated coverage, and the reported quantity is
empirical.

**It may not be strengthened.** Not "first to compute", not "novel method",
not "first in Korea". And it is not yet *earned* — nothing has been built or
measured. Today it is a plan, and must be spoken as one.

---

# THESIS A — if dispatch-by had survived

**Retained only as a record of what was tested.** Full-text comparison did not
support it and it must not be revived without new evidence.

> Protective-action decisions should be made against mission feasibility rather
> than fire position, and the decision-relevant object is the *set* of dispatch
> instants at which an assisted-evacuation round trip still closes.

**Why it failed:** the set representation is SIPP's, since 2011; the latest
departure instant is Kamphuis's, since 2022; whole-traversal hazard is
StochSIPP's definition. Revival requires a documented case where the feasible
*set* and a routing *plan* imply different operational actions, plus evidence
that a non-monotone window actually arises in wildfire geometry.

---

# THESIS B — the fallback, and the one to adopt

> **Assisted wildfire evacuation has a timing budget that nobody has measured.
> Using established latest-departure and safe-interval methods, we quantify —
> for Korean rural communities under a modelled fire with quantified forecast
> error — how much dispatch window exists, how fast it closes, and whether fire
> information arrives soon enough to use it.**

**Contribution type:** `EMPIRICAL_NOVELTY` + `OPERATIONAL_ARTIFACT_NOVELTY`.
Method novelty is explicitly disclaimed.

**Three deliverables, in priority order:**

1. **The dispatch-window measurement.** Feasible dispatch windows for real
   Korean village geometries under modelled spread. Report the window, its
   sensitivity to forecast error, and the event-level Monte Carlo standard
   error *before* any headline number.
2. **The information-vs-expiry comparison (WG-COMB-1).** The one question with
   no identified occupant. Three verified Korean inputs make it computable and
   nobody has done the arithmetic: the operational 5 h/8 h staging, the
   12.9–18.2 min geostationary vs 210–318 min polar-orbit latency gap, and the
   finding that the sub-minute direct-readout tier **does not cover Korea**.
   **Close the S1 search gap before claiming it is unoccupied.**
3. **The tuned-positional-trigger comparator (WG-FV-3).** The only RQ1 leaf
   above UNKNOWN. Its value is evaluative rigour, not novelty — and it is what
   protects deliverables 1 and 2 from the weak-baseline objection.

**What Thesis B concedes, in the first breath:** assisted evacuation, inbound
responder routing, ensemble triggers, forecast value, accuracy-≠-value, OSSE,
latest-departure computation, safe-interval sets, and Korean wildfire
evacuation mapping. All occupied, all conceded before a judge asks.

**What would falsify Thesis B:**
- Dispatch windows turn out to be wide in every realistic scenario → the budget
  is not binding and the measurement is uninteresting.
- Information *always* arrives in time, or *never* does → WG-COMB-1 has no
  interesting structure.
- Travel-time feasibility is not what binds real dispatch (`OPEN_QUESTIONS`
  A4) → the decision variable is wrong, and the vulnerable-populations
  literature currently points this way.

## Confidence and its limits

**Moderate, and bounded by full-text coverage.** Three papers are read at
`METHODS_VERIFIED`, nine at `FULL_TEXT_READ`; **112 of 173 records have no tier
at all**, and `beyki2026modular` — still CRITICAL — has never been read.

Per `NOVELTY_STANDARD.md` §10 no claim here may be held at high confidence.
The occupancy findings are the *robust* part: killing a claim needs one paper,
and Kamphuis, SIPP and Fluschnik were each verified against two independent
sources by the lead. The *surviving* findings are the fragile part, because
they rest on absence, and absence is what our coverage is weakest at
establishing.

**Required disclosures for the surviving empirical claims:**

| | |
|---|---|
| Search coverage | S1–S2; no category reached S3; WG-COMB-1 at S1 only |
| Full-text coverage | 12 of 173 at FULL_TEXT_READ or better; closest RQ2 threat unread |
| Unsearched databases | Scopus, Web of Science, TRID, IEEE Xplore, RISS, DBpia, NDSL; Consensus quota exhausted until 1 Oct |
| Language limitations | Korean pass partial (OpenAlex only; KCI/DBpia blocked); no Japanese, Chinese, Greek, Portuguese or Spanish pass |
| Publication-date cutoff | 2026-09-20 |
| Confidence | Capped at moderate by §10; not high for any claim |

**Next actions, in order:** close the WG-COMB-1 search gap (S1 → S2); sweep
ICAPS/SoCS/AAMAS and the Canadian Traveller Problem for the DBD-4/-5/-6
residues; obtain `beyki2026modular`; retrieve `kamyabniya2022thesis`, whose
time-step structure is the most likely remaining home of a dispatch-feasible
set; run a Japanese pass (避難限界時間, 避難行動要支援者).

**This resolution expires 2026-12-19** (`NOVELTY_STANDARD.md` §7).
